column1: # internal/tui file -> target package assignment (Session 1.5, Phase 0).
# One row per production .go file under internal/tui, one target package each.
# Paths are relative to internal/tui. Columns: path, package, layer, basis.
# `basis` is how the row was decided: `assigned` means the file was read and
# placed by what it declares; `receiver:T` means Go pins it, because a method on
# T cannot cross a package boundary, so the file must land wherever T lands.
# Layers are the graph in context.md: L0 presentation/theme/textfit/taskref/
# status/pulse/keymap, L1 chrome/coordinator, L2 grammar/query, L3 operation,
# L4 route, L5 listsurface, L6 help, L7 notes|taskdetail|taskform|lens|conflict
# then projecthub then outliner, L8 tui (root shell).
# One assignment corrects context.md rather than follow it, and Session 1.6
# should treat it as a finding, not a typo:
#   - outliner_mode.go and outliner_mode_style.go are chrome, not outliner: the
#     mode catalog is vocabulary that operation, route, lens, projecthub and
#     query all read, so it cannot sit at L7.
# Thirteen rows were corrected while their package was being extracted:
#   - due_date_today.go is coordinator, not chrome (Session 2.10). It declares
#     DueDateIsToday alone, which no file in chrome reads; the callers are two
#     coordinator files plus four shell surfaces, all of which reach coordinator.
#     Both packages sit at L1, so leaving it in chrome would have forced the only
#     sideways L1 edge in the graph, coordinator -> chrome, for one function.
#   - view_accent.go is route, not theme (Session 2.1). It resolves a
#     PresentationID to an accent category and only then asks theme for a color,
#     so its whole vocabulary is route's; assigned to theme it was the one file
#     that made an L0 package call upward into L4.
#   - app_errors.go is status, not tui (Session 2.6). It declares errorCmd
#     alone, whose entire body constructs the ErrorMsg that app_messages_core.go
#     already sends to status; leaving it in the shell would have split a
#     message from its only constructor across a package boundary for no gain.
#     Session 2.6's completion contract names the file explicitly.
#   - operational_title.go is pulse, not chrome (Session 2.7). Session 1.5 read
#     it as a header renderer over theme styles and the mode catalog and put it
#     at L1; Session 2.7's completion contract names it as pulse's, and the
#     export budget settles it. The title row is the only reader of the pulse
#     ladder and of TodayPaceReadout, so splitting the two forces
#     and TodayPaceReadout public for one consumer, while keeping them together
#     leaves every one of them unexported. Its one genuine chrome dependency,
#     the mode chip, stayed behind as operationalTitleModeSegment in
#     outliner_mode_style.go, which is where the mode catalog already lives.
#   - cursor.go is chrome, not listsurface (Session 2.8). It declares ClampCursor
#     and HalfPage, two integer functions over a cursor and a window, and its
#     nine production consumers span L2 to L7: grammar's autocomplete.go is one
#     of them, and grammar may import only chrome, theme, textfit and taskref, so
#     at L5 the file was unreachable from its own caller. At L1 every consumer
#   - fullscreen_task_helpers.go is chrome, not taskdetail (Session 2.8). It
#     imports image/color, lipgloss, models, pulse and theme and nothing else,
#     declares the shared full-screen title row and renderPriorityBadge, and is
#     read by text_editor.go, parent_selector.go, tag_add_shared.go and
#     column_layout.go. Session 2.8's brief names it through its
# Eight more rows were corrected by Session 2.8 in the other direction: they
# were assigned chrome but reference identifiers above L1, so they stayed in
# package tui with a corrected row, the shape Session 2.4 established for
#   - contextual_action_sheet.go is listsurface, not chrome. It is built on
#     ListSurfaceModel and thirteen more listsurface types, and reads
#   - operation_text_prompt.go is route, not chrome. It names twelve operation
#     (*AppModel).newOperationTextPrompt, which pins that half to the shell.
#     Session 2.17 corrected this row a second time; see its note below.
#   - parent_selector.go, tag_selector.go and tag_add_shared.go are listsurface,
#     not chrome. All three are ListSurfaceAdapter pickers, and the two tag ones
#   - picker_items.go is query, not chrome. Every declaration left in it is a
#     method on TagInfo, which tag_filter_selector.go declares in query, so Go
#   - view_helpers.go is outliner, not chrome. TitleParams and
#     buildTitleFilterSuffix read query's SortField, SortByDefault and
#   - app_messages_footer_flash.go is tui, not chrome. footerFlashTick reads
#     footerFlashFrameInterval, whose sibling footerFlashFrames lives in the
#     AppModel-pinned footer_flash.go; this is app_errors.go's rule from Session
#     2.6 pointing the other way, keeping a message, its constructor and its two
# Session 2.11 made four moves this table's row shape cannot express, because
# the file's package was right and one declaration inside it was not. Each left
# its file for a package below and got a row of its own:
#     due_format.go as chrome.FormatDeferDate. grammar's capture preview renders
#     a deferral and may not import listsurface, and FormatDueDate, the sibling
#     that reads the same clock, was already chrome's.
#     taskref/task_clone.go. QuickEditSnapshot builds its preview with it, and
#     an L2 package cannot reach L7.
#     filters_common.go (query) for grammar/tag_context_names.go. They are the
#     single-project vocabulary the capture caches read; left in query they
#     would have forced grammar -> query, the one sideways L2 edge that closes a
#     cycle, since query already imports grammar.
#     grammar/deferred_destination.go. Both are parse results: produced in
# Session 2.13 made six more of those declaration-level moves, in both
# directions, and three of them minted a file this table now carries:
#   - The twelve operationFilter* OperationID constants left filter_shortcuts.go
#     (query) for filter_operation_ids.go as operation. A FilterShortcut names
#     the operation its row invokes, so query held the identifiers of a package
#     three layers above it; splitting them out is what let filter_shortcuts.go
#   - The eight *OutlinerModel methods left filter_query_state.go (query) for
#     filter_query_state.go as query's, and activeNarrowingGate is the reason
#     the split had to happen rather than the file staying behind: it branches
#     on hasActiveLens() and reads lensGate and searchGate. Session 4.10 takes
#     that file, not the cited line in the moved one.
#     (query) for outliner_search_gate.go (outliner). The gate needs Today and
#     Next membership, which only the durable plan answers, so query declares
#     the PlanningMembership interface and the Outliner implements it; the
#     compiled destination reads a set it was handed rather than a model it
#     the same open-direct-child census the mode wiring reads, and an L2 package
#     CompletionAgeClauses and ContextFilterClauses. Both are pure clause
#     spellings over query's own vocabulary and sit beside DueFilterClauses,
#     HierarchyFilterClauses and DependencyFilterClauses, which were already
#     filters_common.go as CountTasksWithoutContext. It is the census the
#     no-context picker row counts, over the same BuildTagFacetList population
# Session 2.14 minted four files the same way, all of them splits forced by the
# operation boundary rather than by what a file was assigned:
#   - The sixty-nine operationCore* OperationID constants left
#     checklist refusal names twenty of them and had to move with the registry,
#     while coreInputOperationDescriptors names AppModel-side vocabulary and did
#     not; splitting the identifiers from the descriptors that mint them is what
#     let one cross without the other. They are exported as OperationCore*.
#     for surface_operation_gates.go, staying in the shell. Every entry names a
#     surface input strategy and a surface validator, all of which live above
#     L3, so this half of the file is the one that could not move.
#   - HelpItem left help_types.go (help) for help_item.go. operation_help.go
#     projects descriptors into help rows, so L6 held the struct L3 fills;
#     filteredHelpItem, HelpProvider, helpItemsFromKeyMap and HelpViewModel all
#     stayed behind, since none of them is named below help.
#   - The four picker payload structs and ValueProviderID.AcceptsPresetValue
#     operation_value_payloads.go. Go pins the method to ValueProviderID, and
#     the payloads are the types it asserts against; OperationValueSelectedMsg
#     stayed because it names OperationExecutionRequest, which Session 2.15
# One declaration-level move went the other way: ListCategoryID left
# OperationManifestEntry names a list category so an action sheet can group what
# it lists, which puts the identity below the surface that owns the concept.
# list_surface_types.go keeps the name as an alias, so listsurface's own
# vocabulary is unchanged and no consumer had to be requalified.
# Session 2.16 minted three more identifier files and corrected one row, the
# same two shapes its two predecessors used:
#   - The seventeen operationTask* OperationID constants left
#     task_operation_ids.go, the seven operationSort* left sort_operations.go
#     for sort_operation_ids.go, and the nine project identifiers left
#     project_operation_ids.go. Each donor file is pinned to AppModel or to
#     projecthub, so the identifiers are the only half that could cross; they
#     are exported as OperationTask*, OperationSort*, OperationScope* and
#   - operation_value_provider.go is gone rather than moved. Session 2.14 took
#     its four payload structs, this session took its ten identifiers, and the
#     two messages it had left, OperationValueRequestMsg and
#     operation_executor_types.go. Nothing named after a value provider was
#     still in it, which is what Session 2.15 flagged.
#   - task_operation_manifest.go is tui, not operation. Session 1.5 read it as
#     the manifest projection and put it at L3, but
#     both call outlinerProjectOperationManifest, an L8 identifier, and its six
#     other functions have only shell consumers. Moving it would export twelve
#     names for zero in-package readers; this is the shape Session 2.8
#     established for contextual_action_sheet.go, and Session 2.4 before it for
#     SimplifiedInputStrategy() reaches the root shell through, so cmd/root.go
#     and the root retired_product_vocabulary_test.go compile untouched.
#     surface_operation_gates.go is its production caller, which is what keeps
# Session 2.17 minted one identifier file and corrected one row again:
#   - ProjectHubMode with ProjectHubModeAll and ProjectHubModePinned left
#     project_hub_types.go (projecthub) for route/project_hub_mode.go. It is the
#     one identifier the whole route moving set reads from outside itself:
#     ManageParams carries a ProjectHubMode field and canonicalRouteParams
#     range-checks it, so L4 held a type L7 declared. Nothing else in
#     project_hub_types.go could follow, because the file is pinned to
#     projectHubTaskFilter. All three names were already exported, so the move
#     promotes nothing; projecthub reads them back through route, which its row
#   - operation_text_prompt.go is tui, not route. Session 2.8 moved it out of
#     chrome because it names operation identifiers, and route was the nearest
#     package that could hold them; Session 2.17 read its consumers and found
#     every one of them in the shell -- the AppModel field, app_update_keys.go,
#     app_view_overlays.go, operation_overlay.go and shell.go. Moving it exports
#     OperationTextPromptModel's constructor and its three methods for zero
#     in-package readers, and handleKey and render are the unexported methods
#     the shell's own keyInterceptor and widthRenderer interfaces select on, so
#     the move would rename them on every other overlay too. This is
#   - pipeline_stage.go is not route's, whatever session 2.17's brief lists.
#     This table gives it to listsurface, and its two consumers are both in
#     app_view_status.go, so that row is the listsurface session's to weigh.
# Session 2.19 weighed that row and corrected it:
#   - pipeline_stage.go is tui, not listsurface. It declares pipelineStage and
#     pipelineNextHint, which map a PresentationID to a footer string; neither
#     names a list, a cursor or a row, and no file in the listsurface moving set
#     reads either. Both consumers are in app_view_status.go, so leaving the
#     file in the shell keeps two unexported helpers with their only caller
#     instead of promoting them across a boundary for zero in-package readers.
# Session 2.21 made one declaration-level move and closed one open row:
#     as chrome.JoinGuidanceContext. Supplemental guidance context is guidance
#     vocabulary rather than either caller's: Notes appends the cursor's
#     location to its hints and help_render.go appends the empty-result note,
#     and both must read as one row with one separator. Left in notes it would
#     have forced help -> notes, an edge from L6 into L7.
#   - help_grammar.go is help, as this table has said since Session 1.5, and
#     Session 2.21's completion contract repeating that it "went to grammar in
#     Session 2.11" does not change it. Session 2.11 left the file here and
#     flagged that the reason -- it returns []HelpItem, which help owned -- would
#     have to be revisited if HelpItem moved down. Session 2.14 did move it, to
#     operation at L3, and the answer came out the same way for a stronger
#     reason: grammar is L2, so grammarHelpItems returning []operation.HelpItem
#     would be an upward import the layer fitness test fails on. The file is
#     help's for good, and the grammar it reads is internal/textgrammar.
# Session 2.22 made four declaration-level moves and left five rows standing:
#   - operationKeyDispatch left app_operations.go (tui) for the operation
#     package as operation.KeyDispatch. It is the signature every mounted
#     surface is handed so its browse grammar can resolve, and Notes is the
#     third surface to need it across a package boundary; naming it in the
#     package that owns InputStrategyID and CommandContext is what keeps the
#     shell from exporting a func type for each new tenant.
#   - ManageHubModuleSelectedMsg left manage_hub.go (tui) for route. The Notes
#     location picker raises it, and the module it names is a route.ManageModule
#     already, so the message is route vocabulary; left in the shell it would
#     have forced notes -> tui, the one edge the split forbids.
#   - The tui.note.* OperationID constants left note_operations.go (tui) for
#     notes_input_strategy.go (notes). An operation ID is named by the grammar
#     that binds it, and that grammar sits a package below the registrar.
#     note_operations.go for note_operations_catalog.go (notes), for the same
#     reason one step further: a descriptor is data about a key, and only the
#     handler needs the shell's services. note_operations.go keeps the handler.
#     note_search_index.go and notes_input_strategy_shell.go stay tui, as this
#     table has said since Session 1.5, and Session 2.22's completion contract
#     asking for note_*.go and note_search_index.go does not change it: every
#     one of the five declares *AppModel methods, which Go pins to the shell.
#     There is no combined_notes.go production file; combined_notes_test.go is
#     the whole of that name and it was homed with the manager it exercises.
# Test files are deliberately absent. They follow the production file they
# audit, except the uitest harness and the registry-union parity tests, which
# context.md keeps in the root shell.
